politics.text: Argentine forces seize the Falkland Islands, and Britain sends a naval task force to retake them.
politics.context: The invasion was in April. Britain won the ten-week war and regained the islands in June.

society.text: The warship Mary Rose, pride of King Henry VIII's navy, is lifted from the seabed off Portsmouth after centuries underwater.
society.context: It was raised in October, in front of television cameras. The ship had sunk in 1545, and its contents gave a rich picture of Tudor life.

technology.text: Sony and Philips launch the compact disc, with the first CD players going on sale in Japan.
technology.context: They launched in October. The CD soon replaced vinyl records and cassettes.

arts_culture.text: Michael Jackson releases Thriller, which becomes the best-selling album of all time.
arts_culture.context: It came out in November. The album produced several hit singles, and its title music video was a landmark.

politics.text: Margaret Thatcher's Conservatives win a landslide in Britain's general election, soon after the Falklands War.
politics.context: Labour was split and fought on a hard-left programme, which one of its own MPs called the longest suicide note in history. Thatcher's majority was over a hundred seats.

politics.text: American troops invade the Caribbean island of Grenada after a coup, in an operation condemned by Britain and the United Nations.
politics.context: President Reagan said the aim was to protect American students and restore order. Grenada was a member of the British Commonwealth.

society.text: A Soviet fighter shoots down a Korean Air Lines passenger jet that has strayed into Soviet airspace, killing everyone aboard.
society.context: It was flying from New York to Seoul. The attack sharply raised Cold War tension. Afterwards the United States opened its GPS system for civilian use.

technology.text: President Ronald Reagan announces the Strategic Defense Initiative, a plan for space-based defences against nuclear missiles.
technology.context: Critics nicknamed it Star Wars. It was never fully built, but it alarmed the Soviet Union.

technology.text: The ARPANET switches to TCP/IP, the common language that the modern internet still uses.
technology.context: Every computer on the network had to change over on the same day. This switch is often called the birth of the internet.

arts_culture.text: Michael Jackson performs Billie Jean on television and shows off the moonwalk, a gliding backwards dance step, for the first time.
arts_culture.context: The show, Motown 25, was taped in March and broadcast on NBC in May. Millions of people watched.

arts_culture.text: The final episode of the war comedy M*A*S*H draws a huge American television audience, a record at the time.
arts_culture.context: More than a hundred million people are said to have watched it. The show was set in a medical unit during the Korean War.

politics.text: The Indian prime minister Indira Gandhi is assassinated by two of her Sikh bodyguards in New Delhi.
politics.context: It happened in October. Her son Rajiv became prime minister, and anti-Sikh riots killed thousands.

politics.text: An IRA bomb explodes at a hotel in Brighton during the Conservative Party conference, narrowly missing Margaret Thatcher.
politics.context: Five people were killed. Thatcher carried on with her speech the next day.

society.text: A gas leak at a Union Carbide pesticide plant in Bhopal, India, kills thousands in one of the worst industrial disasters ever.
society.context: It happened in December. Thousands died, and the disaster led to calls for stricter rules on dangerous industries.

society.text: Coal miners across Britain go on strike against pit closures, in a bitter dispute led by Arthur Scargill that lasts a year.
society.context: The strike ended in defeat for the miners the next spring. It changed British industry and politics for decades.

technology.text: Apple launches the Macintosh, a personal computer with a mouse and a graphical screen, after a famous Super Bowl advert.
technology.context: It was launched in January. The advert, directed by Ridley Scott, was shown only once on national television.

arts_culture.text: British and Irish pop stars, led by Bob Geldof and Midge Ure, record Do They Know It's Christmas? for Ethiopian famine relief.
arts_culture.context: The group was called Band Aid. The song was recorded in November and released in December.

politics.text: Mikhail Gorbachev becomes leader of the Soviet Union and begins a programme of reform.
politics.context: He took power in March. His policies of glasnost and perestroika led to the end of the Cold War.

society.text: Rock stars play the Live Aid concerts in London and Philadelphia to raise money for famine victims in Ethiopia.
society.context: The concerts were in July. They raised millions of pounds for famine relief and had a television audience of about two billion.

technology.text: A team led by Robert Ballard finds the wreck of the Titanic on the floor of the North Atlantic.
technology.context: They found it in September. The wreck lay about four kilometres down and had gone undiscovered for over seventy years.

arts_culture.text: The film Back to the Future, in which a teenager travels through time in a car, opens in American cinemas.
arts_culture.context: It opened in July. It was the highest-earning film of the year.

politics.text: Millions of Filipinos take to the streets of Manila in the People Power Revolution, ending Ferdinand Marcos's rule.
politics.context: It took place in February. Corazon Aquino became president, and Marcos fled to Hawaii.

society.text: A reactor explodes at the Chernobyl nuclear power plant in Soviet Ukraine, spreading radioactive fallout across Europe.
society.context: It exploded in April. It was the worst nuclear accident in history, and a large area around the plant was evacuated.

society.text: The American space shuttle Challenger breaks apart shortly after launch, killing all seven crew members.
society.context: It happened in January. The disaster was caused by a faulty seal in a booster rocket.

technology.text: The Soviet Union launches the core module of the Mir space station.
technology.context: It was launched in February. Mir stayed in orbit for fifteen years.

arts_culture.text: Andrew Lloyd Webber's musical The Phantom of the Opera opens in London, starring Michael Crawford and Sarah Brightman.
arts_culture.context: It opened in October. It went on to become the longest-running show in Broadway history.

politics.text: Mass protests in Prague, led by Václav Havel and his Civic Forum, bring down the Communist government of Czechoslovakia.
politics.context: It began in November when police beat students in Prague. Havel, a dissident playwright, became president in December. It is called the Velvet Revolution because almost no blood was shed.

politics.text: Scotland becomes the first part of Britain to charge the poll tax, a flat charge on every adult that replaces local rates.
politics.context: It was brought in a year earlier in Scotland than in England and Wales. It caused riots and helped bring down Margaret Thatcher.

society.text: The tanker Exxon Valdez runs aground in Prince William Sound, Alaska, and spills millions of gallons of crude oil.
society.context: The spill happened in March. It was one of the worst oil spills ever, and devastated wildlife.

society.text: Ninety-seven Liverpool supporters die in a crush at Hillsborough stadium in Sheffield, England.
society.context: It happened in April. The toll was first given as ninety-six.

technology.text: Tim Berners-Lee, a British researcher at CERN in Switzerland, proposes a system for sharing documents through linked pages.
technology.context: He wrote the proposal for the World Wide Web in March. His boss wrote on it: "Vague but exciting."

arts_culture.text: Iran's Ayatollah Khomeini calls for the death of the British novelist Salman Rushdie over his book The Satanic Verses.
arts_culture.context: The fatwa was issued in February. Rushdie was forced into hiding for years.

arts_culture.text: Billy Joel releases We Didn't Start the Fire, a song that races through headlines in a list of names and events.
arts_culture.context: The song runs through news stories from the end of the forties up to the year it was written.

politics.text: Iraq invades Kuwait under Saddam Hussein, setting off a crisis that leads to the Gulf War.
politics.context: The invasion was in August. The United Nations demanded that Iraq withdraw, and a coalition drove it out in 1991.

politics.text: East and West Germany reunite as one country.
politics.context: Reunification took place on the third of October. It came less than a year after the Berlin Wall opened.

society.text: The first McDonald's restaurant in the Soviet Union opens in Pushkin Square, in Moscow, with huge queues.
society.context: It opened in January. The restaurant was the biggest in the world, and customers queued for hours.

technology.text: NASA launches the Hubble Space Telescope aboard the space shuttle Discovery.
technology.context: It was launched in April. Its mirror proved flawed and was repaired three years later.

arts_culture.text: David Lynch's television series Twin Peaks, about the murder of a teenage girl in a small town, begins on American television.
arts_culture.context: It began in April. The strange, dreamlike series became a cult hit.

politics.text: The Soviet Union is dissolved after Mikhail Gorbachev resigns as its president.
politics.context: He resigned on Christmas Day. The Soviet Union broke up into fifteen independent states.

politics.text: A coalition led by the United States begins air strikes on Iraq, opening the Gulf War to free Kuwait.
politics.context: The air campaign began in January. The war ended in February after a ground offensive that took about four days.

society.text: Los Angeles police officers beat the motorist Rodney King, and a bystander films it.
society.context: It happened in March. The acquittal of the officers a year later led to the Los Angeles riots.

technology.text: A Finnish student, Linus Torvalds, announces a free operating system kernel that becomes known as Linux.
technology.context: He announced it in August. Linux now runs most of the world's servers and Android phones.

arts_culture.text: The American band Nirvana releases Nevermind, bringing grunge to a mass audience.
arts_culture.context: It came out in September. The album's success brought alternative rock into the mainstream.

politics.text: Twelve European countries sign the Maastricht Treaty, creating the European Union.
politics.context: They signed in February. The treaty paved the way for the euro and the European Union as it exists today.

society.text: Barcelona hosts the Summer Olympic Games.
society.context: They opened in July. They were the first Summer Games without a boycott since 1972.

technology.text: A British engineer, Neil Papworth, sends the first text message, "Merry Christmas", to a mobile phone.
technology.context: The message was sent in December. It went from a computer to a mobile phone on the Vodafone network.

arts_culture.text: Disney's animated film Aladdin, with a genie voiced by Robin Williams, is released.
arts_culture.context: It was released in November. It was the highest-earning film of the year.

politics.text: Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organization sign the Oslo Accords on the White House lawn.
politics.context: The signing was in September. Yitzhak Rabin and Yasser Arafat shook hands, but the peace process later collapsed.

society.text: A powerful earthquake strikes the state of Maharashtra, in western India, killing thousands.
society.context: The Latur earthquake struck in September. About ten thousand people died, in a region where such a quake was not expected.

technology.text: Students at the University of Illinois release Mosaic, a web browser that brings pictures to the internet.
technology.context: It was released in April. Mosaic helped make the web popular with the public.

arts_culture.text: Steven Spielberg's film Jurassic Park, with dinosaurs made from computer graphics, is released.
arts_culture.context: It opened in June. It was the highest-earning film ever made at that time.

politics.text: Nelson Mandela is sworn in as South Africa's first Black president after the country's first all-race elections.
politics.context: He took office in May. Mandela formed a government of national unity.

society.text: Hutu extremists begin a genocide in Rwanda, killing hundreds of thousands of Tutsi in about a hundred days.
society.context: It began in April. The world was widely criticised for failing to stop the killing.

technology.text: Queen Elizabeth II and French president François Mitterrand open the Channel Tunnel, linking Britain and France by rail.
technology.context: It opened in May. The tunnel is about fifty kilometres long and runs under the English Channel.

technology.text: Netscape releases Navigator, a web browser that brings the internet to millions of ordinary people.
technology.context: The full version came out in December. Netscape's share sale the next year set off the internet boom.

arts_culture.text: Quentin Tarantino's film Pulp Fiction wins the top prize at the Cannes Film Festival.
arts_culture.context: It won in May. Tarantino's film broke the rules of storytelling and revived John Travolta's career.

politics.text: Israeli prime minister Yitzhak Rabin is assassinated by an extremist after a peace rally in Tel Aviv.
politics.context: It happened in November. The killer opposed the peace deal with the Palestinians.

society.text: A powerful earthquake strikes the Japanese city of Kobe, killing thousands.
society.context: It struck in January. More than six thousand people died, in Japan's worst earthquake in decades.

technology.text: Jeff Bezos launches Amazon, selling books online, from a garage in Seattle.
technology.context: It opened to the public in July. Amazon began as an online bookshop.

arts_culture.text: Pixar's film Toy Story, the first feature made entirely with computer animation, is released.
arts_culture.context: It opened in November. It was Pixar's first feature film, and a huge success.

politics.text: The Taliban capture Kabul and take control of most of Afghanistan.
politics.context: They took the city in September. They ruled most of Afghanistan until 2001.

society.text: A bomb explodes in a park during the Summer Olympic Games in Atlanta, Georgia.
society.context: It exploded in July. One person was killed and over a hundred were injured.

technology.text: NASA launches the Mars Pathfinder mission, which will land a small rover called Sojourner on Mars.
technology.context: It was launched in December. Sojourner explored the surface of Mars the next year.

arts_culture.text: The film Trainspotting, about young heroin users in Edinburgh, is released in Britain.
arts_culture.context: It was released in February. The film launched Ewan McGregor's career and made a cult of its soundtrack.

politics.text: Britain hands Hong Kong back to Chinese rule at midnight, ending more than a century of colonial control.
politics.context: The handover took place on the first of July. China promised to keep Hong Kong's way of life under "one country, two systems".

society.text: Thailand lets its currency, the baht, float, setting off a financial crisis across Asia.
society.context: The Asian financial crisis began in July. It spread to Indonesia and South Korea and cost millions of jobs.

society.text: Diana, Princess of Wales, dies in a car crash in a Paris road tunnel, and Britain goes into mass mourning.
society.context: She died on the last day of August. Her funeral was watched by millions around the world.

technology.text: IBM's computer Deep Blue defeats the reigning world chess champion, Garry Kasparov, in a six-game match in New York.
technology.context: The match ended in May. It was the first time a computer beat a reigning world champion in a match.

technology.text: Scientists at the Roslin Institute, in Scotland, announce Dolly, the first mammal cloned from an adult cell.
technology.context: Dolly was cloned from a mammary gland cell, so she was named after the singer Dolly Parton. She was born in July 1996 and died in 2003.

arts_culture.text: The British author J. K. Rowling publishes Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone, a book about a boy wizard, in a small first print run.
arts_culture.context: It came out in June, from the publisher Bloomsbury. It became one of the best-selling book series in history.

politics.text: Political parties in Northern Ireland sign the Good Friday Agreement, ending decades of conflict known as the Troubles.
politics.context: It was signed in April. It set up a power-sharing government in Northern Ireland.

society.text: Hurricane Mitch hits Central America, killing thousands in Honduras and Nicaragua.
society.context: It struck in October. About eleven thousand people died.

technology.text: Two Stanford students, Larry Page and Sergey Brin, found the search company Google in California.
technology.context: They founded it in September. The company grew out of a research project at Stanford.

arts_culture.text: James Cameron's film Titanic wins eleven Academy Awards, equalling the record.
arts_culture.context: The Oscars ceremony was in March. It tied the record held by Ben-Hur.

politics.text: Vladimir Putin is elected president of Russia, after Boris Yeltsin resigns and names him acting leader.
politics.context: Putin was a former KGB officer and had been Yeltsin's last prime minister.

politics.text: Vicente Fox wins Mexico's presidential election, ending more than seventy years of rule by one party.
politics.context: Fox, a former Coca-Cola executive, led the National Action Party. The old ruling party was the PRI.

politics.text: After mass protests in Belgrade, Yugoslav president Slobodan Milošević is forced to give up power.
politics.context: Protesters stormed the parliament building. Milošević was later put on trial for war crimes in The Hague.

society.text: The Russian nuclear submarine Kursk sinks in the Barents Sea, killing all the crew despite a long rescue effort.
society.context: One hundred and eighteen men died. President Putin was criticised for being slow to respond and for refusing foreign help at first.

society.text: A Concorde supersonic airliner crashes after taking off from Paris, killing everyone aboard and some people on the ground.
society.context: It was the first fatal crash of a Concorde. The plane was withdrawn from service three years later.

technology.text: Scientists announce the first draft of the human genome, a map of all the genes in a human being, at the White House.
technology.context: The announcement was made by President Clinton, with the leaders of two rival research teams. A finished version followed in 2003.

technology.text: The first crew arrives at the International Space Station, beginning a continuous human presence in space.
technology.context: The crew were two Russians and an American. People have lived on the station without a break ever since.

arts_culture.text: Charles M. Schulz, creator of the comic strip Peanuts and its Charlie Brown and Snoopy, dies the night before his last strip appears.
arts_culture.context: Peanuts had run for almost fifty years, and Schulz drew every strip himself. He died at home in California.

politics.text: American and British forces begin air strikes on Afghanistan, after the attacks of the previous month.
politics.context: The strikes began in October. The Taliban were driven from power within weeks.

society.text: The energy company Enron files for bankruptcy, the largest in American history at the time.
society.context: It filed in December. Its collapse followed an accounting scandal.

technology.text: Apple releases the iPod, a pocket-sized digital music player.
technology.context: It was released in October. Apple advertised it as "a thousand songs in your pocket".

arts_culture.text: The French romantic comedy Amélie, set in Paris, is released and becomes a hit around the world.
arts_culture.context: It was released in April. The film was nominated for five Oscars.

politics.text: East Timor becomes the first new country of the century, as it celebrates full independence after years of Indonesian rule.
politics.context: A United Nations mission had run the territory since a vote for independence. The country took the name Timor-Leste.

politics.text: In his State of the Union speech, President George W. Bush names Iran, Iraq and North Korea as an axis of evil.
politics.context: The phrase was used to justify tougher policies. The invasion of Iraq followed the next year.

society.text: The Boston Globe begins publishing its investigation into the sexual abuse of children by Catholic priests and its cover-up by the Church.
society.context: The reports, by the Globe's Spotlight team, led to hundreds of cases and the resignation of Cardinal Bernard Law. They were later made into the film Spotlight.

society.text: The Winter Olympic Games open in Salt Lake City, Utah, under tight security.
society.context: They were the first Olympics after the attacks of September the Eleventh. The opening ceremony included a flag recovered from the World Trade Center.

technology.text: Mark Shuttleworth, a South African internet entrepreneur, becomes the first African in space, as a paying space tourist.
technology.context: He flew on a Russian Soyuz to the International Space Station. He later founded the company behind the Ubuntu computer system.

arts_culture.text: The Tribute in Light begins, two columns of blue light rising over Manhattan where the Twin Towers stood.
arts_culture.context: It was first lit on the six-month anniversary of the attacks of September the Eleventh. It proved so popular that it returned every year.

politics.text: An American-led coalition invades Iraq and topples Saddam Hussein.
politics.context: The invasion began in March. No weapons of mass destruction were found.

society.text: The American space shuttle Columbia breaks apart on re-entry over Texas, killing all seven astronauts.
society.context: It happened on the first of February. The shuttle had been damaged by foam during launch.

technology.text: Scientists announce that the Human Genome Project has finished mapping the human genome.
technology.context: The announcement was in April, fifty years after the discovery of DNA's structure.

arts_culture.text: Peter Jackson's film The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King premieres in Wellington, New Zealand.
arts_culture.context: The premiere was in December. The film later won eleven Oscars.

politics.text: The Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat dies in a military hospital near Paris.
politics.context: He died in November. Arafat had led the Palestinians for decades.

politics.text: Viktor Yushchenko wins Ukraine's presidency after mass protests overturn a rigged election, in the Orange Revolution.
politics.context: The rerun vote was in December. Protesters had worn orange, the colour of the movement.

society.text: A huge undersea earthquake off Sumatra triggers a tsunami that kills more than two hundred thousand people around the Indian Ocean.
society.context: It struck on the day after Christmas. The waves hit countries from Indonesia to Africa.

technology.text: The Harvard student Mark Zuckerberg launches Facebook from his university dormitory.
technology.context: It launched in February. Facebook began as a site for Harvard students.

arts_culture.text: Pixar's animated film The Incredibles, about a family of superheroes in hiding, is released.
arts_culture.context: It was released in November. It won the Oscar for best animated feature.

politics.text: The former Lebanese prime minister Rafic Hariri is killed by a huge car bomb in Beirut.
politics.context: The attack was in February. It led to protests that forced Syrian troops out of Lebanon.

society.text: A powerful earthquake strikes Kashmir, killing tens of thousands of people in Pakistan and India.
society.context: It struck in October. About eighty thousand people died.

society.text: Hurricane Katrina floods much of New Orleans, Louisiana, and kills more than a thousand people.
society.context: It struck at the end of August. The flooding was made worse by failures in the city's levees.

technology.text: Three former PayPal employees launch YouTube, a site for sharing videos, in California.
technology.context: It was founded in February. Google bought it the next year.

arts_culture.text: The Taiwanese director Ang Lee's film Brokeback Mountain, about two cowboys in love, is released.
arts_culture.context: It was released in December. It won three Oscars, including best director.

politics.text: Saddam Hussein, Iraq's former dictator, is hanged in Baghdad after being convicted of crimes against humanity.
politics.context: He was convicted of the killing of 148 Shia men in the town of Dujail. The execution was filmed and caused controversy.

politics.text: Hezbollah fighters capture two Israeli soldiers in a cross-border raid, and Israel responds with a month-long war in Lebanon.
politics.context: The war killed more than a thousand Lebanese civilians. A United Nations ceasefire ended it in August.

society.text: A strong earthquake strikes the Indonesian city of Yogyakarta and the area around it, killing thousands of people.
society.context: More than five thousand people died. The quake struck early in the morning, and the ancient temple of Prambanan was damaged.

society.text: Italy win the football World Cup in Germany, beating France on penalties after the French captain is sent off for a head-butt.
society.context: Zinedine Zidane's head-butt on Marco Materazzi came in extra time of the final in Berlin.

technology.text: Astronomers vote to strip Pluto of its status as a planet and class it as a dwarf planet.
technology.context: The International Astronomical Union voted at a meeting in Prague. Its new rules said that a planet must clear the space around its orbit.

technology.text: The social network Twitter is founded in San Francisco, with messages limited to a few characters.
technology.context: The first message was sent in March by Jack Dorsey. The service opened to the public in July.

arts_culture.text: The Finnish monster rock band Lordi win the Eurovision Song Contest in Athens with Hard Rock Hallelujah.
arts_culture.context: The band wore monster masks on stage. It was Finland's first win in the contest.

politics.text: Buddhist monks lead mass protests against the military government of Myanmar, in what is called the Saffron Revolution.
politics.context: The protests ran from August to October. The army crushed them.

society.text: Customers queue outside Northern Rock branches in Britain, in the first run on a British bank in over a century.
society.context: The run began in September. The government had to guarantee savers' deposits.

technology.text: Apple, led by Steve Jobs, puts the first iPhone, a touchscreen phone with no physical keyboard, on sale in the United States.
technology.context: It launched in June, five months after Jobs unveiled it. It changed the phone industry.

arts_culture.text: J. K. Rowling's final Harry Potter novel, The Deathly Hallows, is released and sells millions of copies on its first day.
arts_culture.context: It was published in July. It sold about eleven million copies in the first day.

politics.text: Barack Obama is elected the first Black president of the United States.
politics.context: Obama beat the Republican John McCain, as the global financial crisis deepened. He took office in January 2009.

society.text: A huge earthquake in Sichuan province, in China, kills about seventy thousand people.
society.context: It struck in May. Many schools collapsed, which led to anger about poor construction.

society.text: The investment bank Lehman Brothers collapses in the largest bankruptcy in American history, deepening the global financial crisis.
society.context: It filed in September. The firm had been in business for over a century.

society.text: Zimbabwe's hyperinflation peaks, as prices double almost every day and shoppers carry banknotes in bundles to buy basic goods.
society.context: In mid-November, monthly inflation reached about 79.6 billion per cent, by one economist's estimate. Notes worth 100 billion Zimbabwe dollars were printed, and the currency was dropped soon after.

technology.text: Scientists at CERN, near Geneva, switch on the Large Hadron Collider, the most powerful particle accelerator ever built.
technology.context: The first beams circulated in September. A fault stopped the machine for over a year.

arts_culture.text: Beijing opens the Summer Olympics with a vast ceremony at the Bird's Nest stadium, directed by Zhang Yimou.
arts_culture.context: The ceremony was held in August. It featured two thousand and eight drummers.

politics.text: Thousands of Iranians protest in Tehran after a disputed presidential election, in what becomes known as the Green Movement.
politics.context: The protests began in June after a vote that opposition supporters said had been rigged. Security forces crushed them, but the movement became a symbol of opposition to the regime.

society.text: A passenger jet makes an emergency landing on the Hudson River in New York, and everyone on board survives.
society.context: It happened in January, after birds struck both engines. Captain Chesley Sullenberger landed the plane on the water, and all 155 people on board survived.

society.text: Iceland's last McDonald's restaurants close, after the country's banking crash made imported ingredients too costly.
society.context: It happened at the end of October. A man bought a burger and fries on the last day and kept them. They have barely rotted, and are still on display in Iceland, with a webcam.

technology.text: A programmer using the name Satoshi Nakamoto starts the Bitcoin network by creating its first block.
technology.context: It started in January. Bitcoin was the first successful decentralised digital currency, and its first block contained a newspaper headline about bank bailouts.

arts_culture.text: James Cameron's film Avatar opens, and goes on to become the highest-earning film in history.
arts_culture.context: It opened in December. It became the first film to earn more than two billion dollars, and it pioneered modern 3D cinema.

politics.text: A Tunisian street vendor, Mohamed Bouazizi, sets himself on fire in protest, sparking unrest that spreads across the Arab world.
politics.context: The act was in December. The unrest became known as the Arab Spring.

society.text: A huge earthquake devastates Haiti and its capital, Port-au-Prince.
society.context: It struck in January. Estimates of the number of dead range from about one hundred thousand to over three hundred thousand.

society.text: Thirty-three Chilean miners are rescued after more than two months trapped deep underground.
society.context: They were brought up in October, after sixty-nine days. The rescue was shown live to a worldwide television audience.

technology.text: Apple's Steve Jobs unveils the iPad, a tablet computer, in San Francisco.
technology.context: It was unveiled in January and went on sale in April. The iPad made tablet computers popular.

arts_culture.text: Dubai opens the Burj Khalifa, the tallest building in the world.
arts_culture.context: It opened in January. At more than eight hundred metres, it was the tallest building in the world.

politics.text: Egypt's long-ruling president Hosni Mubarak resigns in Cairo after eighteen days of mass protests.
politics.context: He stepped down in February, during the Arab Spring. He had ruled for almost thirty years.

politics.text: Libyan rebels capture Sirte, and Colonel Muammar Gaddafi is killed after months of civil war.
politics.context: He was killed in October after being found hiding in a drainpipe. His death ended over four decades of rule.

society.text: A huge undersea earthquake off the coast of Japan triggers a tsunami and a nuclear emergency at Fukushima.
society.context: The Tōhoku earthquake struck in March. The tsunami killed about eighteen thousand people and damaged the Fukushima nuclear plant.

technology.text: IBM's computer system Watson defeats two human champions on the American television quiz show Jeopardy!
technology.context: The win came in February. Watson had to answer questions in natural language, and it beat the show's best human players.

technology.text: Apple unveils Siri, a voice assistant, on its new iPhone.
technology.context: It was unveiled in October. Siri brought voice commands to millions of phones.

arts_culture.text: The British singer Adele releases her second album, which tops the sales charts in many countries.
arts_culture.context: The album is titled 21. Its hits included Rolling in the Deep and Someone Like You, and it was the best-selling album of the year in the world.

politics.text: Mohamed Morsi is elected president of Egypt after the revolution that toppled Hosni Mubarak.
politics.context: He won in June, in the country's first free presidential election. The army removed him a year later.

society.text: London hosts the Summer Olympic Games, with an opening ceremony directed by the film-maker Danny Boyle.
society.context: They opened in July. The ceremony included a film in which Queen Elizabeth II appeared alongside James Bond.

technology.text: NASA's rover Curiosity lands on Mars after a daring "sky crane" descent.
technology.context: It landed in August. The car-sized rover was sent to find out whether Mars could ever have supported life.

technology.text: Scientists at CERN, near Geneva, announce the discovery of a particle consistent with the Higgs boson.
technology.context: They announced it in July. Peter Higgs and François Englert, who had predicted the particle, shared the Nobel Prize in 2013.

arts_culture.text: The South Korean singer Psy releases "Gangnam Style", whose video becomes the first to reach a billion views.
arts_culture.context: It was released in July. The video became the first on YouTube to pass a billion views, in December.

politics.text: The Argentine cardinal Jorge Bergoglio is elected pope, taking the name Francis, the first pope from the Americas.
politics.context: He was elected in March, after Pope Benedict XVI resigned. He was the first Jesuit pope.

society.text: A powerful typhoon, Haiyan, devastates the Philippines, killing thousands.
society.context: It struck in November. It was one of the strongest storms ever to hit land, and killed more than six thousand people.

technology.text: Scientists announce that the Voyager probe has left the Sun's bubble and entered interstellar space.
technology.context: NASA made the announcement in September. The probe had actually crossed into interstellar space a year earlier.

technology.text: Edward Snowden, an American intelligence contractor, leaks documents revealing mass government surveillance.
technology.context: The first stories appeared in June. The leaks started a worldwide debate about privacy and spying.

arts_culture.text: The French electronic duo Daft Punk release Random Access Memories, an album that wins the major prizes.
arts_culture.context: It came out in May and won several Grammy awards. The album's hit single was "Get Lucky".

politics.text: Russia annexes the Crimean peninsula from Ukraine, after troops without insignia take control.
politics.context: The annexation was in March, after a disputed referendum. Most countries did not recognise it, and sanctions on Russia followed.

society.text: A Malaysia Airlines jet disappears over the Indian Ocean with everyone on board, in one of aviation's great mysteries.
society.context: It vanished in March, on a flight from Kuala Lumpur to Beijing. Despite a huge search, the aircraft's main wreckage was not found.

technology.text: The European probe Rosetta lands a small craft, Philae, on a comet.
technology.context: The landing was in November, after a ten-year journey. The craft bounced and ended up in a shadowed spot, but still sent back data.

arts_culture.text: Richard Linklater's film Boyhood, shot over twelve years with the same cast, premieres.
arts_culture.context: It premiered in January. The film was shot over twelve years, and won an Oscar for Patricia Arquette.

politics.text: David Cameron's Conservatives win a surprise majority in Britain's election, ending five years of coalition with the Liberal Democrats.
politics.context: Polls had predicted a hung parliament. Ed Miliband resigned as Labour leader. The SNP won almost every seat in Scotland.

politics.text: Greece elects the left-wing Syriza party, led by Alexis Tsipras, on a promise to end austerity.
politics.context: Syriza was the first radical left party to win power in a euro country. Months of tense talks with Greece's creditors followed.

society.text: Gunmen attack the Paris office of the satirical magazine Charlie Hebdo and kill twelve people.
society.context: The attackers said they were avenging cartoons of the Prophet. Millions marched in France in the days afterwards.

society.text: A powerful earthquake strikes Nepal, killing about nine thousand people and damaging historic buildings in Kathmandu.
society.context: It struck in April, and caused an avalanche on Mount Everest. Many of the old temples in Kathmandu's Durbar Square were wrecked.

society.text: The United States Supreme Court rules that same-sex couples have the right to marry in every state, in Obergefell v. Hodges.
society.context: The decision was by five votes to four, and Justice Anthony Kennedy wrote the main opinion. It was handed down in June. Some states had already allowed same-sex marriage.

society.text: A photo of a dress goes viral online, as millions argue over whether it is blue and black or white and gold.
society.context: The photo was posted on social media in February. Scientists later studied why people see different colours, and linked it to how the brain judges the lighting in a picture.

technology.text: Apple releases the Apple Watch, its first smartwatch, which tracks fitness and shows messages on a small screen on the wrist.
technology.context: It went on sale in April, after being announced the previous September. It soon became one of the best-selling watches in the world.

arts_culture.text: Star Wars returns in The Force Awakens, with Daisy Ridley as the scavenger Rey, and breaks box office records within days.
arts_culture.context: It was the first Star Wars film made after Disney bought Lucasfilm, and the first in ten years. Harrison Ford returned as Han Solo. It opened in December.

politics.text: The Colombian government and the FARC guerrillas sign a peace deal to end more than fifty years of conflict.
politics.context: The first deal was signed in September and rejected by voters. A revised deal followed in November.

politics.text: British voters choose to leave the European Union in a referendum.
politics.context: The vote was in June. About fifty-two per cent voted to leave, and David Cameron resigned as prime minister.

society.text: Rio de Janeiro hosts the Summer Olympic Games, the first held in South America.
society.context: They opened in August. The Games came as Brazil faced a deep economic and political crisis.

technology.text: Google's AlphaGo program beats the Go champion Lee Sedol in Seoul, South Korea.
technology.context: The match was in March. AlphaGo won four games to one.

arts_culture.text: The American songwriter Bob Dylan is awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.
arts_culture.context: The prize was announced in October. Dylan was the first musician to win it, praised for creating new poetic expressions within the American song tradition.

politics.text: Theresa May calls a snap general election to win a bigger majority, but loses her majority and has to rely on the Democratic Unionists.
politics.context: She called it in April, expecting a landslide, but the Conservatives lost seats. Jeremy Corbyn's Labour did far better than the polls had predicted. The result was a hung parliament.

politics.text: Zimbabwe's army takes control of the country, and Robert Mugabe, who had ruled for almost four decades, resigns days later.
politics.context: The army acted after Mugabe sacked his vice-president Emmerson Mnangagwa, who became president. Mugabe had led Zimbabwe since independence in 1980.

politics.text: Catalonia holds an independence referendum that Spain's courts have banned, and police use force to stop people voting.
politics.context: The Catalan government said most voters backed independence. The Catalan parliament declared independence in October, and Madrid took direct control of the region.

politics.text: Emmanuel Macron, a former banker and economy minister with a brand-new party, is elected president of France.
politics.context: He beat the far-right candidate Marine Le Pen in the second round in May. At thirty-nine, he became the youngest president in French history.

society.text: A suicide bomber attacks a pop concert by Ariana Grande at an arena in Manchester, killing more than twenty people, many of them young.
society.context: The attack happened as the audience was leaving. Many of the victims were children and teenagers.

society.text: At Kuala Lumpur airport, Kim Jong-nam, half-brother of North Korea's leader, is poisoned with a nerve agent and dies.
society.context: The poison was VX, one of the deadliest nerve agents. Two women were charged with the killing.

technology.text: Apple releases the iPhone X, a phone with no home button that unlocks with a scan of the user's face.
technology.context: It went on sale in November. The X, the Roman numeral for ten, marked ten years since the first iPhone.

technology.text: Epic Games releases Fortnite Battle Royale, a free online game in which a hundred players fight until one is left standing.
technology.context: Epic had already released a different Fortnite mode earlier in the year. The free battle royale mode, added in September, became one of the most popular games in the world.

technology.text: Nintendo releases the Switch, a games console that can be used at home on a television or carried as a handheld.
technology.context: The Switch was an unexpected success and became one of the best-selling consoles ever.

technology.text: SpaceX launches a rocket booster that has already flown to space once, the first reuse of an orbital-class rocket.
technology.context: Landing and reusing boosters cut the cost of launches. The booster had flown a mission the year before.

arts_culture.text: Despacito, a Spanish-language hit by Luis Fonsi and Daddy Yankee, breaks streaming records and tops the charts around the world.
arts_culture.context: A remix with Justin Bieber helped it reach number one in the United States. It was released in January.

arts_culture.text: At the Oscars, La La Land is wrongly announced as best picture, and then Moonlight is revealed as the true winner.
arts_culture.context: The presenters, Warren Beatty and Faye Dunaway, were handed the wrong envelope. The cast of La La Land were already on stage making speeches when the mistake was found.

politics.text: The leaders of North and South Korea meet at Panmunjom and sign a declaration promising peace.
politics.context: They met in April. Kim Jong-un became the first North Korean leader to cross into the South.

society.text: Twelve boys and their football coach are rescued from a flooded cave in Thailand, after more than two weeks.
society.context: The rescue was in July. Divers brought the boys out over three days, and a former Thai navy diver died during the operation.

technology.text: SpaceX launches Falcon Heavy, the most powerful rocket of its day, with a sports car as a test cargo.
technology.context: It was launched in February. Two of its side boosters landed back on Earth at the same time.

arts_culture.text: Marvel's film Black Panther, set in the African kingdom of Wakanda, is released.
arts_culture.context: It was released in February. It was the first superhero film to be nominated for the Oscar for Best Picture.

politics.text: The long-serving Algerian president Abdelaziz Bouteflika resigns after weeks of mass street protests.
politics.context: He resigned in April, after twenty years in power. The protests, which began over his plan to run again, continued afterwards.

society.text: Fire engulfs the roof and spire of Notre-Dame cathedral in Paris.
society.context: The fire was in April. The spire collapsed, but the main structure survived.

technology.text: Astronomers with the Event Horizon Telescope release the first ever image of a black hole, in a distant galaxy.
technology.context: The image was released in April. The galaxy is Messier 87.

arts_culture.text: The South Korean director Bong Joon-ho's film Parasite wins the Palme d'Or at Cannes.
arts_culture.context: It won in May. It later won the Oscar for best picture.

politics.text: The Taliban retake Kabul as the Afghan government collapses and Western troops withdraw.
politics.context: They entered the city in August, as the president fled. It ended a twenty-year war.

society.text: The container ship Ever Given runs aground in the Suez Canal and blocks it for nearly a week.
society.context: It was stuck in March. Hundreds of ships were held up.

technology.text: NASA's small helicopter Ingenuity makes the first powered flight on another planet, on Mars.
technology.context: It flew in April. Its flights proved that powered flight is possible in the thin air of Mars.

arts_culture.text: The South Korean television series Squid Game is released and becomes a global hit.
arts_culture.context: It was released in September. It became Netflix's most-watched series at the time.

politics.text: Sri Lanka's president Gotabaya Rajapaksa flees the country as protesters storm his residence in Colombo.
politics.context: He fled in July, during an economic crisis. He later resigned.

politics.text: Russia launches a full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
politics.context: The invasion began in late February. It started Europe's largest war in decades.

society.text: Qatar hosts the football World Cup, and Argentina, led by Lionel Messi, beat France on penalties in the final.
society.context: The final was in December. It is widely seen as one of the best finals ever.

technology.text: The American company OpenAI releases ChatGPT, a chatbot that writes fluent text, to the public.
technology.context: It was released at the end of November. It reached one hundred million users within about two months.

arts_culture.text: S. S. Rajamouli's Indian film RRR, a Telugu-language action epic, is released and finds a huge global audience.
arts_culture.context: It was released in March. Its song "Naatu Naatu" won an Oscar in 2023.

politics.text: Syria's president Bashar al-Assad flees to Russia as rebels take Damascus, ending his family's long rule.
politics.context: It happened in December, after a rapid rebel offensive. His family had ruled for more than fifty years.

society.text: Paris hosts the Summer Olympic Games, with an opening ceremony held along the River Seine.
society.context: The Games opened in July. The ceremony was held outdoors along the river, instead of in a stadium.

technology.text: SpaceX catches a returning Super Heavy booster with giant mechanical arms on its launch tower.
technology.context: It happened in October. It was a step towards making the giant rocket reusable.

arts_culture.text: The film Wicked, based on the Broadway musical about the witches of Oz, is released.
arts_culture.context: It was released in November. The film covers the first half of the stage musical.
